mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows arbitrary permissions to be added; the permission matrix becomes unconstrained. The LeastPrivilege assertion checks that permissions are strictly defined per the contract. FR-023 and FR-024 depend on specific permission denials. Injecting an unauthorized permission (e.g., Applicant -> PatchApplicationStatus) forces a violation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_UnauthorizedPermission { Applicant -> PatchApplicationStatus in PermMatrix.allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this constraint allows multiple in-flight applications for the same applicant. The assertion checks that at most one application per applicant can be in Pending or UnderReview status simultaneously. Injecting two in-flight apps for the same applicant violates this invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_TwoInFlightApps { some disj app1, app2: LoanApplication, u: User | app1.applicant = u and app2.applicant = u and app1.status in Pending + UnderReview and app2.status in Pending + UnderReview }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact permits an officer to be assigned to an application they themselves are the applicant on. This violates the no-self-assignment invariant (FR-010) and the no-self-mutation pattern. Injecting a self-assigned application directly violates both assertions.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_SelfAssignment { some app: LoanApplication, u: User | app.applicant = u and app.assignedOfficer = u }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows audit entries to be created without required fields or to exist in a mutable state. The assertion checks that all audit entries have the core fields (application, actor, actorRole, newStatus). Without this constraint, the append-only invariant is violated. Injecting an audit entry with missing fields forces the violation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_IncompleteAuditEntry { some ae: AuditEntry | no ae.actor or no ae.actorRole or no ae.newStatus }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact permits applicants to access other applicants' applications. The assertion checks that non-owning applicants cannot retrieve applications they don't own. Injecting permission for one applicant to view another applicant's application violates the invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_InfoLeakage { some disj u1, u2: User, app: LoanApplication | Applicant in u1.userRoles and Applicant in u2.userRoles and u1 != u2 and app.applicant = u2 and (u1 -> GetApplicationById in PermMatrix.allowed) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this constraint allows a user to simultaneously hold both Officer and Auditor roles, which violates the mutually-exclusive role constraint. The assertion checks that no user has both roles. Injecting a user with both roles forces the violation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_ConflictingRoles { some u: User | Officer in u.userRoles and Auditor in u.userRoles }
